payload.report: Skin biopsy showing a monomorphic perivascular/adnexal atypical T-cell infiltrate with aberrant CD4/CD8 coexpression and abnormal flow cytometry, together with splenomegaly and lymphadenopathy, strongly supports T-cell lymphoma with secondary vasculitic ulceration. Doppler ultrasound indicating venous stasis as secondary and pathological exclusion of Behçet disease/primary vasculitis/thrombotic APS refute alternative hypotheses. However, TCR gene rearrangement and bone marrow studies are unavailable, so T-cell clonality is not definitively confirmed; the diagnosis is favored but not proven. No further subtyping is possible from current evidence.
